title: Orchestration probe runner for VPC priming and model verification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a deterministic, repeatable post-deploy probe runner that can be invoked as part of the Terraform/AWS/On‑prem deployment flow for VPC/private installs. Current post-deploy checks are ad-hoc: separate scripts, manual SSH, or one-off CI jobs. This ticket implements an orchestration service and Terraform hooks that execute a curated sequence of readiness probes against the freshly deployed control and data plane.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module triggers the probe-runner after apply (or on demand) and returns non-zero on failure.
Probe sequence covers: API handshake & schema validation, auth token exchange (customer KMS/STS), model artifact load verification, lightweight tokenized generation smoke, and throughput ramp check.
Probe-runner emits structured results to Console (probe-event logs) and to the deployment S3/DB for retention and automated triage.
Failure classification: transient retry vs blocking failure; blocking failures prevent marking deploy as healthy and emit a routed PagerDuty alert if configured.
Playbook and runbook pages link to remediation steps and a debug bundle collected automatically on failure.
Automation works for both cloud-hosted VPC and on‑prem packaging (the same probe logic, pluggable transport layer).
Minimal blast radius: probes only use a service account with least privilege and temporary keys; no customer data is exfiltrated during checks.
implementation_tasks: Design probe sequence DSL and YAML schema (probe types: http, grpc, model-load, kv-check, throughput-ramp, cache-verify)
Add Terraform module hooks that call the probe-runner via AWS SSM RunCommand or a private cluster job (k8s Job/ECS RunTask) depending on deployment mode
Implement probe-runner service (Go) with plugin-style probe executors, timeouts, and exponential backoff retry logic
Model warmup executor: load model weights, run N small sample inferences, compare token-level metrics and latency against baseline tolerances
Integrate probe output with Console events API and a lightweight JSON artifact stored in deployment bucket for history
Create GitHub Action workflow to run the probe-runner against ephemeral test VPCs for PR validation
Add tests: unit for probe executors, e2e that spins up a minimal reference deployment and validates probe outcomes
test_plan: Unit tests for each probe type with mocks for RPC/HTTP and synthetic model backends
E2E harness: a reference VPC stack in CI that the probe-runner targets; baseline acceptance: API handshake < 250ms, first-token latency < 450ms, model warmup success 3/3 samples
Throughput smoke: ramp to 10 concurrent generator connections for 30s, 95th percentile latency < 800ms for small prompts
Failure injection: simulate model artifact missing and ensure probe-runner marks failure and uploads debug bundle
Security test: ensure the probes operate using short-lived credentials and cannot list S3 buckets beyond the deployment artifact prefix
blockers: Service account RBAC for on‑prem orchestration is not finalized (need least-privilege policy from Security)
Private registry auth for CI runners (container images) requires token rotation support
Model artifact signing verification path not gated into probe-runner yet (waiting on ENG-92500 to finish)
notes: Opted to run warmup as a separate probe executor to keep failures visible and actionable (warmup failures should not be conflated with API handshake failures)
Will expose a --dry-run flag on the Terraform module to validate probe DSL without mutating remote state
Decided to publish probe artifacts as JSONL to S3 with keys: deployments/<deploy-id>/probes/<timestamp>.jsonl for easy diagnostic retrieval
We will parameterize thresholds per-customer in the Terraform var file; defaults will come from the runtime perf baseline matrix
